history.summary: A compact 484 sqft 1BR at Treasure at Tampines, $795K / $1,643 PSF — ~9% below the $1,806 URA median, on a huge 1,007-txn series (resale-adjusted +4.25%/yr). Sub-$800K quantum and mega-development liquidity are pluses, but the 2,203-unit scale creates persistent internal resale competition and the 1.12km MRT walk is poor.
history.rating_rationale: PSF $1,643 is ~9% under the $1,806 median and the appreciation read is the most data-rich in the batch (1,007 txns; system already discounted new-launch bias to +4.25%/yr resale-only). But Treasure is Singapore's largest condo (2,203 units) — there is always supply on the resale market, so individual units compete hard on price and a tiny 484 sqft 1BR is the most commoditised stack. Simei MRT 1.12km (13-min walk) is weak. Liquid and fairly priced, but not differentiated.
red_flags: 2,203-unit mega-development — constant internal resale supply caps per-unit pricing power
Simei MRT 1.12km / 13-min walk — poor connectivity for a 1BR tenant
Small 484 sqft shoebox — most commoditised unit type with the project
New-launch bias flagged (raw 4.96% trimmed to 4.25% resale-only)
catalysts: CRL + DTL extension and Tampines Regional Centre strengthen the broader OCR demand
Extensive resort-style facilities and family demand from the mega-project scale
Below-median entry PSF on a deep, reliable data series

history.summary: Treasure at Tampines 3BR, 915 sqft at $1.635M / $1,787 psf — the cheapest of 7 live 915s and the only Treasure 3BR asking below its own same-size 12-month median ($1,812 psf, n=19). But the cushion is only ~1.4%, the project trades at a PREMIUM to every 99-yr D18 peer, and the floor is unknown on a stack where floors 1-5 print $96/psf below floors 11-15 — so the apparent discount may be a low-floor artifact, not value.
history.rating_rationale:
SAME-SIZE BENCHMARK (the number that decides this). The $1,740 all-size resale median is NOT the comp — it mixes 61 sub-600sqft shoeboxes into a 3BR question. Against the correct band: 915 sqft resales are $1,738 psf/24mo (n=49), $1,812/12mo (n=19), $1,834/6mo (n=6); 950-1200 sqft are $1,780/24mo (n=52), $1,853/12mo (n=22). PropertyGuru's own 3BR project average ($1,859, 12mo) corroborates. So this $1,787 ask is +2.8% vs 24mo, -1.4% vs 12mo, -2.6% vs 6mo — sitting at the 26th percentile of the last 12 months' 915-sqft prints. A thin cushion, not a discount.

THE HEADLINE LISTING IS DEAD. Listing 500036576 (1,033 sqft, $1.66M, $1,607 psf, score 729) was last seen 2026-06-07 and did not reappear in the 2026-07-28 poll. The DB shows it relisted as 500191291 at $1,950,000 / $1,888 psf (same unit_group |3|350, relisted_from=500036576) — a +17.5% re-ask. Its $1,607 psf was ~14% below the 1,033-sqft 12mo median of $1,858 (n=17), i.e. genuinely cheap, and it is gone. The live 1,033 ask is now $1.95M, outside budget. (Separately: three of the four candidate IDs in the brief — 500148020, 500075341, 500182744 — are Treasure CREST, a D19 EC in Sengkang, not this project.)

WHAT THE PROJECT ACTUALLY IS. Priced at a premium to its district, not a discount: across D18's 850-1150 sqft resale band over 24 months, Treasure's $1,747 median psf (n=99) is the HIGHEST of any 99-yr project in the district — The Tapestry $1,696 (n=35), Coco Palms $1,692 (n=19), The Palette $1,533, Alps $1,506, Waterview $1,491, D'Nest $1,485. Age-adjusted it lands at par (relative_value: -0.9% vs D18 age-adjusted median). So the repo's single most robust forward signal, cheap-vs-district-peers, is ABSENT here. What remains is region (OCR, realized fwd +3.7%/yr) and exceptional liquidity — both real, neither unique to this asset.

RESALE-PROFIT PICTURE FROM THE URA BOOK (realsmart unavailable — see note). 1,007 prints, 435 resales, resale window 2024-03 to 2026-05; the sub-sale wave ended 2024-03 so the project is now purely resale-driven. Launch-cohort gains, same-size: 915 sqft New Sale median $1,425 psf ($1.304M, n=42) -> 12mo resale $1,812 ($1.658M) = +27% over ~5 yrs, ~+4.9%/yr. 1,033 sqft: $1,537 -> $1,858 = +21%, ~+3.9%/yr. Resale-to-resale for the 3BR band by half-year: 2024H1 $1,718 (n=36), 2024H2 $1,716 (n=39), 2025H1 $1,771 (n=36), 2025H2 $1,834 (n=24), 2026H1 $1,836 (n=13) = +6.9% over 24 months, ~+3.4%/yr — at or just under the OCR baseline, not above it. The launch-cohort +4.9%/yr is not repeatable: it was earned buying at $1,425 psf from the developer; a resale buyer today starts at $1,787.

PRICE UP, VOLUME DOWN. 3BR-band resales: 84 in Apr-24..Mar-25 -> 54 in Apr-25..Mar-26 (-36%). All-size resales 214 (2024) -> 170 (2025) -> ~120 annualised (2026). Prices kept rising into falling volume, which is where the cushion should be widening and isn't.

MONTHS OF INVENTORY. 19 live 3BR PropertyGuru listings on the 2026-07-28 poll; collapsing certain duplicates (identical price + sqft, different agent: the $1.938M/1012 pair and the $2.200M/1087 pair) gives ~16-17 distinct units. Against 3BR-band velocity of 4.5/month (54 over the lag-safe 12mo) that is 3.6-3.8 months of inventory; against the last lag-safe 6 months (18 prints, 3.0/month) it is 5.3-5.7 months. Verdict: the mega-project's scale genuinely does buy liquidity — this is not a clogged book — but the trend is the wrong way, and 7 of the 16 are 915-sqft units competing directly with this one at $1.635M-$1.850M. Caveat: PropertyGuru capture is partial, so this is a floor on true inventory.

BED COUNT: CLEAN. bed_bands --check returns ok — Treasure's URA rental filings put a 3BR at 850-1050 sqft (median 950) on 242 contracts, and 915 sits mid-band. No 2BR+study mislabel here. (Note the 818-sqft asks sit below the band's p5, passing only on the 12% tolerance — those are the most compact 3BR format and carry a bedroom_sqft_mismatch ingest flag.)

MRT: MARKETING IS WRONG, THE PENALTY IS REAL. OneMap block coordinates put the 29 blocks 493-857m straight-line from Simei EW3 (median block 642m, 706m to Exit A) and 824-1,199m from Tampines West DT31. But the road/path network roughly doubles it: PropertyGuru's pedestrian routing gives 13 min / 1.12 km to Simei and OSRM's network route is longer still. Marketing sites claiming a '600m, 8-10 min sheltered walk to Simei' are quoting the straight line, not a walkable route. MMR's -4.62 MRT component is earned.

CRL DOES NOT SERVE THIS PROJECT. Tampines North (CR6, opening 2030) sits under Tampines Ave 11 at the Ave 6 / Tampines North Dr 2 junction — roughly 1.9 km north of Treasure and on the far side of the PIE. It is the catalyst for Parktown Residence, which is built on top of it, not for Treasure. Treating the CRL as a Treasure catalyst (as the June-2026 eval of the 1BR did) is a misread.

SUPPLY LANDS INSIDE THE HOLD WINDOW. Parktown Residence (1,193 units, sold at ~$2,360 psf, TOP ~2027), Aurelle of Tampines EC (TOP 2028) and Pinery Residences (Tampines St 94 GLS, ~587 units, $2,100-2,400 psf indicative, previewing 2026) all complete or start reselling in 2027-2030 — precisely the owner's 2031-2033 exit window. The offset is real but modest: new stock at $2,100-2,400 psf makes Treasure's $1,787 look cheap on a headline basis (relative_value: -14.0% vs new-launch-implied fair), and Treasure's ~$1.6M quantum sits well under theirs. The risk is the tenant/buyer at the margin choosing an MRT-integrated 2027 building over a 2023 non-MRT one.

FLOOR UNKNOWN — THIS CAPS THE CALL. floor_level and facing are ~0% populated (scraper bug fixed only 2026-07-29, so no historical record carries them). It matters a lot here: 915-sqft prints over 24 months run $1,702 psf on floors 1-5 (n=20), $1,760 on 6-10 (n=21), $1,798 on 11-15 (n=8) — a 5.6% spread. If this unit is floors 1-5 its fair comp is $1,702 psf = $1.557M and the $1.635M ask is a 5% PREMIUM, not a discount. Being the cheapest of 7 live 915s at only the 26th percentile of prints is itself weak evidence of a low floor or a compromised stack (PIE-facing north edge, west-sun corner, or one of the majority of units that face another block — the project's documented headline weakness). Confidence is medium, not high, for exactly this reason.

WHY NEUTRAL AND NOT BUY. Deep liquidity (1,007 prints, 2,203 units, buyer_pool deep) and OCR region are genuine positives; the entry is fair, the bed count is clean, and the quantum fits the mandate. But there is no margin of safety at $1,787 psf, no project-specific catalyst inside the hold window (the CRL belongs to a competitor), a permanent 16+ unit internal 3BR shelf to clear on exit, and the 2023-TOP 0-5yr cohort penalty. On a ~3.4%/yr resale-to-resale trend, five years of gross appreciation (~+18%) barely clears BSD ($54,850) plus ~2.5% exit friction — call it +2-3%/yr net. That is a hold-the-market outcome, not a resale-profit trade.

WHY NOT AVOID. It is not overpriced and it is not illiquid — 49 same-size prints in 24 months make this the best-price-discovered 3BR in D18. Buying here is unlikely to lose money; it is unlikely to make a profit worth the mandate.

WHERE IT BECOMES A BUY. At <= $1,570,000 ($1,715 psf) with a VERIFIED floor 8+ and a non-PIE, non-west-corner stack. That is the 12-month minimum print ($1,716 psf) and the 24-month p25 ($1,710 psf, n=49) — a genuine ~5% cushion below the 12mo median that would survive the floor uncertainty. Roughly a 4% negotiation off the current $1.635M, on a listing that has not moved its price since 2026-06-07. If the floor comes back as 1-5, the number drops to $1,520,000 ($1,661 psf) and the trade is probably not worth doing at all.
red_flags: No margin of safety: $1,787 psf is only 1.4% under the 915-sqft 12-month median ($1,812, n=19) and +2.8% over the 24-month median ($1,738, n=49) — priced, not cheap.

Floor and facing unknown (~0% populated). 915-sqft prints span $1,702 (floors 1-5) to $1,798 (floors 11-15) — if this is a low floor the ask is a 5% PREMIUM, not a discount. Being the cheapest of 7 live 915s is weak evidence it IS a low floor or compromised stack.

Project trades at the HIGHEST 3BR-band psf of any 99-yr D18 project ($1,747 vs Tapestry $1,696, Palette $1,533, Waterview $1,491) — the repo's most robust forward signal, cheap-vs-peers, is absent (age-adjusted -0.9%, i.e. at par).
Volume falling into rising prices: 3BR-band resales 84 (Apr24-Mar25) -> 54 (Apr25-Mar26), -36%; all-size 214 (2024) -> 170 (2025) -> ~120 annualised.

16-17 distinct live 3BR listings, 7 of them the same 915-sqft format at $1.635M-$1.850M = 3.6-5.7 months of inventory and permanent internal competition on exit. 2,203 units means this never goes away.
The CRL is not a catalyst for this project: Tampines North (CR6, 2030) is ~1.9 km north across the PIE, built under Parktown Residence — a competitor, not this site.
Marketing claim of '600m / 8-10 min to Simei' is the straight line (median block 642m); the real pedestrian route is ~1.12 km / 13 min. No station at the doorstep on either line.
Supply lands inside the exit window: Parktown Residence (1,193u, TOP ~2027), Aurelle EC (TOP 2028), Pinery Residences (~587u, previewing 2026) all resell into 2027-2033.
2023 TOP = the 0-5yr post-TOP cohort, historically the worst forward-return band (mitigated by the cheap ~$1,346 psf launch, so little launch premium left to amortise).

Documented project weaknesses: tight 3-row layout means most units face another block (privacy is the headline complaint), PIE noise on the north edge, heavy afternoon sun on west-corner stacks, mixed management feedback.
3.16% gross yield on a $4,300 URA-based rent — carry is thin; the 5-7yr return has to come almost entirely from price.

Genuine liquidity from scale — 1,007 URA prints, 2,203 units, ~8-10%/yr turnover; the exit takes months, not years, which is the real payoff of the mega-project format.
OCR region — the repo's realized forward-return leader (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1, CCR +1.9).
-14.0% vs new-launch-implied fair value; Parktown at ~$2,360 psf and Pinery at $2,100-2,400 psf reset the district's anchor upward and make a $1,787 psf 3BR the value option on quantum.
$1.635M quantum sits in the deep HDB-upgrader band and under the owner's $1.8M ceiling with room for entry costs.
93 years of lease remaining — no decay drag inside a 5-7yr hold.
Tampines Regional Centre employment base underpins tenant demand (225 rental contracts in 6 months per portal data).
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: 3.16% gross / 1.97% net on a $4,300/mo URA project-and-bed-derived rent (confidence 0.95). Consistent with the ~3.6% portal figure on a lower price basis. Well below the 5.5% artifact threshold, so no verification concern — but it is carry, not appreciation, and per the repo's own backtest higher yield actually predicts LOWER forward price growth. At this level the 5-7yr return is a price bet, not an income one. Tenant demand is deep (a large project in Tampines Regional Centre's catchment) but the 1.1 km MRT walk caps achievable rent versus Tampines-proper stock.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 4.23% model rate is resale-only and de-biased, and it is defensible as a story — but the project's OWN resale-to-resale 3BR-band record is +3.4%/yr (2024H1 $1,718 -> 2026H1 $1,836 psf), not 4.23%. The higher launch-cohort figure (915 sqft: $1,425 psf New Sale -> $1,812 psf 12mo resale = +4.9%/yr) is not available to a buyer entering at $1,787. Per the repo's priors, trailing CAGR has ~zero forward power once clustered, so I am NOT overriding the rate — but I am treating ~3.4%/yr as the realistic planning number, which after BSD ($54,850) and ~2.5% exit friction leaves roughly +2-3%/yr net over five years. Momentum is -0.609 and volume is down 36% year-on-year, which argues against extrapolating the 2025H2-2026H1 psf jump.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Layout matched with high confidence (sqft delta 0.0%) to the 3BR type, 915 sqft — the volume 3BR (59 lifetime prints, 49 in 24 months), 2 baths, ~85 sqm. Stack and floor are NOT known: floor_level and facing are ~0% populated repo-wide. This matters more than usual here. The site is 29 identical 12-storey blocks in three east-west rows, and the profile flags three ways a unit can be compromised — the north-edge row (blocks 43-57) faces the PIE, west-corner stacks (123, 117, 116, 110, 7, 1, 92, 26, 27, 79, 186, 187, 199) take heavy afternoon sun, and the tight three-row spacing means the majority of units look directly into another block. The middle row (blocks 15-35), which faces the internal 50m lap pools on both sides, is the one to want. 24-month 915-sqft prints by floor: $1,702 psf (01-05, n=20), $1,760 (06-10, n=21), $1,798 (11-15, n=8). Before offering, get the unit number: floor, row and facing swing the fair value of this exact listing by ~5.6%, which is four times the apparent discount.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: No override. Model rate 4.23% (ura_resale_only, 1,007 txns) retained per repo priors that trailing CAGR carries ~zero forward power; the project's own 3BR-band resale-to-resale trend of ~+3.4%/yr is used as the planning number in the narrative instead.
agent_evaluation.realsmart_note: UNAVAILABLE — not estimated, not guessed. realsmart_cache.py --show 'Treasure At Tampines' resolves the slug correctly (https://realsmart.sg/p/treasure-at-tampines, resolved=true, source='p') but returns ok=false with every metric null: realscore, pct_profitable, annual_return_pct, resale_txns, avg_holding_yrs, total_transactions all null. Only street ('Tampines Lane') and tenure ('99 to 101 years') came back. The /map SPA fallback was previously tried and also returned empty. The REALSCORE downside lens is therefore ABSENT for this evaluation and has been substituted with a direct read of the URA book (1,007 prints / 435 resales in data/ura_district_D18.csv): same-size-band psf by half-year, launch-cohort vs current-resale gain, and 3BR-band transaction velocity. Do not read the nulls as a low score.
